title: Write your own behavior
summary: Write a behavior in JavaScript from an example, see it update as you save, and give it settings of its own.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
The behaviors in the Behaviors panel are small JavaScript files, and you can write your own the same way: a name, its settings, and a function that says how to move the instance on each frame.

You don't need to know much JavaScript; you will start from a working example. Click Next to begin.

steps.title: Select the ball
steps.text: Press V for the Selection tool and click the ball on the stage.

steps.title: Open the Behaviors panel
steps.text: Choose Window > Behaviors if it is not showing. It lists what is on the selection and the settings of each.

steps.title: Start a new behavior
steps.text:
Click Add Behavior and choose New Behavior... at the bottom. Call it Drift.

Phoenix writes an example behavior into your Behaviors folder and opens it in the script editor.

steps.title: Read the example
steps.text:
The file calls behavior({...}) with:

  • name and description, as the panel shows them;
  • params, its settings, each becoming a slider;
  • evaluate(ctx, p), run for each frame: ctx says which frame and time it is, p holds the settings.

It returns what to add to the instance: here x grows with time, and y bobs up and down.

steps.title: Add it
steps.text: Back in Phoenix, click Add Behavior and choose Drift, now in the list. Play: the ball drifts right, bobbing.

steps.title: Change the code
steps.text:
In the script editor, change Math.sin(ctx.time * 2) to Math.sin(ctx.time * 6) and save with Ctrl+S.

Phoenix reads the file again as soon as it is saved: the ball bobs faster. An error shows in the Output panel, and the ball stays where its keys put it.

steps.title: Give it a setting
steps.text:
Add a setting for how fast it bobs. In params, after bob, add:

rate: { label: "Bobs per second", value: 1, min: 0, max: 10, step: 0.1 }

and use it: Math.sin(ctx.time * 2 * Math.PI * p.rate). Save, and a Bobs per second slider appears in the panel.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You wrote a behavior, changed it live, and gave it a setting.

ctx has more: random() and noise() for steady randomness, keyedAt() for the keyed motion on other frames, other() for other instances, loudness() for the soundtrack. Return {copies: [...]} to make copies. See Help and the Behaviors page for the whole list. Your behaviors are in Add Behavior > Open Behaviors Folder.
